passages.text: If a man marries a woman, but she becomes displeasing to him because he finds some indecency in her, he may write her a certificate of divorce, hand it to her, and send her away from his house.
passages.sermon:
A man marries a woman.
He becomes her husband.
He finds something indecent in her.
She no longer pleases him.
He writes her a certificate of divorce.
He gives the certificate to her.
He sends her away from his house.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ יִקַּ֥ח אִ֛ישׁ אִשָּׁ֖ה וּבְעָלָ֑הּ וְהָיָ֞ה אִם־ לֹ֧א תִמְצָא־ חֵ֣ן בְּעֵינָ֗יו כִּי־ מָ֤צָא בָהּ֙ עֶרְוַ֣ת דָּבָ֔ר וְכָ֨תַב לָ֜הּ סֵ֤פֶר כְּרִיתֻת֙ וְנָתַ֣ן בְּיָדָ֔הּ וְשִׁלְּחָ֖הּ מִבֵּיתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: If, after leaving his house, she goes and becomes another man’s wife, and the second man hates her, writes her a certificate of divorce, hands it to her, and sends her away from his house, or if he dies, then the husband who divorced her first may not remarry her after she has been defiled, for that is an abomination to the LORD. You must not bring sin upon the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
passages.sermon:
A woman may leave her first husband's house.
She may marry another man.
If her second husband hates her, he may write her a certificate of divorce.
He may give the certificate to her.
He may send her away from his house.
If the second husband dies, she becomes free from him.
The first husband who divorced her may not marry her again.
She has become defiled.
This is an abomination before the LORD.
You must not bring sin upon the land.
The LORD your God is giving you this land as an inheritance.
passages.original: וְיָצְאָ֖ה מִבֵּית֑וֹ וְהָלְכָ֖ה וְהָיְתָ֥ה לְאִישׁ־ אַחֵֽר׃ וּשְׂנֵאָהּ֮ הָאִ֣ישׁ הָאַחֲרוֹן֒ וְכָ֨תַב לָ֜הּ סֵ֤פֶר כְּרִיתֻת֙ וְנָתַ֣ן בְּיָדָ֔הּ וְשִׁלְּחָ֖הּ מִבֵּית֑וֹ א֣וֹ כִ֤י יָמוּת֙ הָאִ֣ישׁ הָאַחֲר֔וֹן אֲשֶׁר־ לְקָחָ֥הּ ל֖וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃ לֹא־ יוּכַ֣ל בַּעְלָ֣הּ הָרִאשׁ֣וֹן אֲשֶֽׁר־ שִׁ֠לְּחָהּ לָשׁ֨וּב לְקַחְתָּ֜הּ לִהְי֧וֹת ל֣וֹ לְאִשָּׁ֗ה אַחֲרֵי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֻטַּמָּ֔אָה כִּֽי־ תוֹעֵבָ֥ה הִ֖וא לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹ֤א תַחֲטִיא֙ אֶת־ הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁר֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לְךָ֖ נַחֲלָֽה׃ס

passages.text: If a man is newly married, he must not be sent to war or be pressed into any duty. For one year he is free to stay at home and bring joy to the wife he has married.
passages.sermon:
A man marries a new wife.
He must not go out with the army.
No one may require him to do any duty.
He is free to stay at home for one year.
He must bring joy to his wife whom he has married.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ יִקַּ֥ח אִישׁ֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה חֲדָשָׁ֔ה לֹ֤א יֵצֵא֙ בַּצָּבָ֔א וְלֹא־ יַעֲבֹ֥ר עָלָ֖יו לְכָל־ דָּבָ֑ר נָקִ֞י יִהְיֶ֤ה לְבֵיתוֹ֙ שָׁנָ֣ה אֶחָ֔ת וְשִׂמַּ֖ח אֶת־ אִשְׁתּ֥וֹ אֲשֶׁר־ לָקָֽח׃ס

passages.text: Do not take a pair of millstones or even an upper millstone as security for a debt, because that would be taking one’s livelihood as security.
passages.sermon:
A millstone is a tool for grinding grain.
People use millstones to make food.
Do not take a pair of millstones as a pledge for a debt.
Do not take even the upper millstone as a pledge.
If you take a millstone, you take away a person’s means to live.
Taking a millstone as security is taking someone’s livelihood.
passages.original: לֹא־ יַחֲבֹ֥ל רֵחַ֖יִם וָרָ֑כֶב כִּי־ נֶ֖פֶשׁ ה֥וּא חֹבֵֽל׃ס

passages.text: If a man is caught kidnapping one of his Israelite brothers, whether he treats him as a slave or sells him, the kidnapper must die. So you must purge the evil from among you.
passages.sermon:
A man may kidnap another man from among the Israelites.
He may treat the kidnapped man as a slave.
He may sell the kidnapped man.
If someone catches the kidnapper, the kidnapper must die.
You must remove this evil from among you.
passages.original: כִּי־ יִמָּצֵ֣א אִ֗ישׁ גֹּנֵ֨ב נֶ֤פֶשׁ מֵאֶחָיו֙ מִבְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְהִתְעַמֶּר־ בּ֖וֹ וּמְכָר֑וֹ וּמֵת֙ הַגַּנָּ֣ב הַה֔וּא וּבִֽעַרְתָּ֥ הָרָ֖ע מִקִּרְבֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: In cases of infectious skin diseases, be careful to diligently follow everything the Levitical priests instruct you. Be careful to do as I have commanded them.
passages.sermon:
This command is about infectious skin diseases.
God gives this command to the people of Israel.
God tells the people to be very careful about these diseases.
The people must listen to the Levitical priests.
The Levitical priests will give instructions about what to do.
The people must do everything the priests say.
God has commanded the priests what to teach.
The people must obey all that God has commanded through the priests.
passages.original: הִשָּׁ֧מֶר בְּנֶֽגַע־ הַצָּרַ֛עַת לִשְׁמֹ֥ר מְאֹ֖ד וְלַעֲשׂ֑וֹת כְּכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁר־ יוֹר֨וּ אֶתְכֶ֜ם הַכֹּהֲנִ֧ים הַלְוִיִּ֛ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּיתִ֖ם תִּשְׁמְר֥וּ לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃ס

passages.text: Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam on the journey after you came out of Egypt.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your God.
Miriam was a woman among the Israelites.
You came out of Egypt with the Israelites.
You traveled on a journey after leaving Egypt.
The LORD your God did something to Miriam during that journey.
Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam.
passages.original: זָכ֕וֹר אֵ֧ת אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֛ה יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ לְמִרְיָ֑ם בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ בְּצֵאתְכֶ֥ם מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃ס

passages.text: When you lend anything to your neighbor, do not enter his house to collect security.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel laws for lending to others.
God commanded these laws through Moses.
If you lend anything to your neighbor, you must follow these laws.
Do not go into your neighbor’s house to take a pledge.
Do not enter his home to collect security for the loan.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ תַשֶּׁ֥ה בְרֵֽעֲךָ מַשַּׁ֣את מְא֑וּמָה לֹא־ תָבֹ֥א אֶל־ בֵּית֖וֹ לַעֲבֹ֥ט עֲבֹטֽוֹ׃

passages.text: You are to stand outside while the man to whom you are lending brings the security out to you.
passages.sermon: When you lend something to another person, you must not enter his house to take security.\r\nYou must stand outside.\r\nThe man who owes you will bring the security out to you.
passages.original: בַּח֖וּץ תַּעֲמֹ֑ד וְהָאִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר אַתָּה֙ נֹשֶׁ֣ה ב֔וֹ יוֹצִ֥יא אֵלֶ֛יךָ אֶֽת־ הַעֲב֖וֹט הַחֽוּצָה׃

passages.text: If he is a poor man, you must not go to sleep with the security in your possession; be sure to return it to him by sunset, so that he may sleep in his own cloak and bless you, and this will be credited to you as righteousness before the LORD your God.
passages.sermon:
This law speaks about lending to a poor man.
The poor man gives you something as security for a loan.
You must not keep his security overnight.
You must return the security to him by sunset.
He needs his cloak to sleep in at night.
If you return it, he will bless you.
God will see this as righteousness for you.
The LORD your God will count it as a good deed.
passages.original: וְאִם־ אִ֥ישׁ עָנִ֖י ה֑וּא לֹ֥א תִשְׁכַּ֖ב בַּעֲבֹטֽוֹ׃ הָשֵׁב֩ תָּשִׁ֨יב ל֤וֹ אֶֽת־ הַעֲבוֹט֙ כְּבֹ֣א הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ וְשָׁכַ֥ב בְּשַׂלְמָת֖וֹ וּבֵֽרֲכֶ֑ךָּ וּלְךָ֙ תִּהְיֶ֣ה צְדָקָ֔ה לִפְנֵ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃ס

passages.text: Do not oppress a hired hand who is poor and needy, whether he is a brother or a foreigner residing in one of your towns.
passages.sermon:
God commands you.
Do not oppress a hired worker.
This worker is poor and needy.
He may be your brother.
He may be a foreigner.
He may live in your land.
He may live in your town.
passages.original: לֹא־ תַעֲשֹׁ֥ק שָׂכִ֖יר עָנִ֣י וְאֶבְי֑וֹן מֵאַחֶ֕יךָ א֧וֹ מִגֵּרְךָ֛ אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּאַרְצְךָ֖ בִּשְׁעָרֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: You are to pay his wages each day before sunset, because he is poor and depends on them. Otherwise he may cry out to the LORD against you, and you will be guilty of sin.
passages.sermon:
God commands you to treat poor workers fairly.
A poor man works for you.
He depends on his wages to live.
You must pay him his wages on the same day he works.
You must pay him before the sun goes down.
If you do not pay him, he may cry out to the LORD against you.
If he cries out, you will be guilty of sin.
passages.original: בְּיוֹמוֹ֩ תִתֵּ֨ן שְׂכָר֜וֹ וְֽלֹא־ תָב֧וֹא עָלָ֣יו הַשֶּׁ֗מֶשׁ כִּ֤י עָנִי֙ ה֔וּא וְאֵלָ֕יו ה֥וּא נֹשֵׂ֖א אֶת־ נַפְשׁ֑וֹ וְלֹֽא־ יִקְרָ֤א עָלֶ֙יךָ֙ אֶל־ יְהוָ֔ה וְהָיָ֥ה בְךָ֖ חֵֽטְא׃ס

passages.text: Fathers shall not be put to death for their children, nor children for their fathers; each is to die for his own sin.
passages.sermon:
God gave this law to Israel.
God said that each person is responsible for his own actions.
A father must not be put to death for his child’s sin.
A child must not be put to death for his father’s sin.
Each person must die only for his own sin.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ יוּמְת֤וּ אָבוֹת֙ עַל־ בָּנִ֔ים וּבָנִ֖ים לֹא־ יוּמְת֣וּ עַל־ אָב֑וֹת אִ֥יש בְּחֶטְא֖וֹ יוּמָֽתוּ׃ס

passages.text: Do not deny justice to the foreigner or the fatherless, and do not take a widow’s cloak as security.
passages.sermon:
God commands you to act justly.
Do not deny justice to the foreigner.
Do not deny justice to the fatherless.
Do not take a widow’s cloak as security.
passages.original: לֹ֣א תַטֶּ֔ה מִשְׁפַּ֖ט גֵּ֣ר יָת֑וֹם וְלֹ֣א תַחֲבֹ֔ל בֶּ֖גֶד אַלְמָנָֽה׃

passages.text: Remember that you were slaves in Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you from that place. Therefore I am commanding you to do this.
passages.sermon:
You were slaves in Egypt.
The LORD your God redeemed you from Egypt.
Remember this.
Because of this, I am commanding you to do this thing.
passages.original: וְזָכַרְתָּ֗ כִּ֣י עֶ֤בֶד הָיִ֙יתָ֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם וַֽיִּפְדְּךָ֛ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ מִשָּׁ֑ם עַל־ כֵּ֞ן אָנֹכִ֤י מְצַוְּךָ֙ לַעֲשׂ֔וֹת אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּֽה׃ס

passages.text: If you are harvesting in your field and forget a sheaf there, do not go back to get it. It is to be left for the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel laws to protect the vulnerable.
God commanded the people to care for foreigners, orphans, and widows.
If you harvest your field and forget a sheaf in the field, do not return to take it.
Leave the forgotten sheaf.
The foreigner, the orphan, and the widow may take it.
God wants you to do this so that He may bless you in all the work of your hands.
passages.original: כִּ֣י תִקְצֹר֩ קְצִֽירְךָ֨ בְשָׂדֶ֜ךָ וְשָֽׁכַחְתָּ֧ עֹ֣מֶר בַּשָּׂדֶ֗ה לֹ֤א תָשׁוּב֙ לְקַחְתּ֔וֹ לַגֵּ֛ר לַיָּת֥וֹם וְלָאַלְמָנָ֖ה יִהְיֶ֑ה לְמַ֤עַן יְבָרֶכְךָ֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ בְּכֹ֖ל מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָדֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: When you beat the olives from your trees, you must not go over the branches again. What remains will be for the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow.
passages.sermon:
God gave this command to Israel.
God rescued Israel from slavery in Egypt.
When you harvest olives from your trees, do not go over the branches a second time.
Leave what remains on the tree.
The leftover olives belong to the foreigner.
The leftover olives belong to the fatherless.
The leftover olives belong to the widow.
passages.original: כִּ֤י תַחְבֹּט֙ זֵֽיתְךָ֔ לֹ֥א תְפָאֵ֖ר אַחֲרֶ֑יךָ לַגֵּ֛ר לַיָּת֥וֹם וְלָאַלְמָנָ֖ה יִהְיֶֽה׃ס

passages.text: When you gather the grapes of your vineyard, you must not go over the vines again. What remains will be for the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow.
passages.sermon:
God gave laws to Israel.
God told the people how to harvest their vineyards.
If you gather grapes from your vineyard, do not go back over the vines again.
Leave what remains on the vines.
Leave these grapes for the foreigner.
Leave them for the fatherless.
Leave them for the widow.
passages.original: כִּ֤י תִבְצֹר֙ כַּרְמְךָ֔ לֹ֥א תְעוֹלֵ֖ל אַחֲרֶ֑יךָ לַגֵּ֛ר לַיָּת֥וֹם וְלָאַלְמָנָ֖ה יִהְיֶֽה׃

passages.text: Remember that you were slaves in the land of Egypt. Therefore I am commanding you to do this.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God reminds them of their past.
You were slaves in the land of Egypt.
You suffered and had no freedom.
God rescued you from slavery.
Because of this, God gives you a command.
God commands you to do this thing.
passages.original: וְזָ֣כַרְתָּ֔ כִּי־ עֶ֥בֶד הָיִ֖יתָ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם עַל־ כֵּ֞ן אָנֹכִ֤י מְצַוְּךָ֙ לַעֲשׂ֔וֹת אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּֽה׃ס
